paper.title_en: Testing Departures from the $Λ$CDM model in f(T) Gravity with DESI DR2
paper.abstract_en: Recent analyses combining DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements with other cosmological observations have reported indications of departures from the $Λ$CDM model within dynamical dark energy scenarios. We investigate whether such deviations are reproduced consistently in $f(T)$ gravity and whether they persist when different cosmological observations are combined. Using the DESI DR2 BAO measurements, Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), and Pantheon+ Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia) sample, we constrain three representative $f(T)$ models: the power-law, exponential, and hyperbolic-tangent models. We compare the constraints obtained from different combinations of data, distinguishing changes in marginalized parameter distributions from changes in the relative statistical performance of the models. For the power-law model, the mild deviation from the $Λ$CDM model obtained from BAO+CMB disappears after the SNe Ia data are included. In contrast, the exponential model retains a preference for a nonzero deformation parameter in the full analysis, while the allowed parameter space of the hyperbolic-tangent model changes substantially after the CMB distance priors are included. Importantly, the parameter-level deviation found for the exponential model does not lead to a clear statistical preference over the $Λ$CDM model according to the information criteria, whereas the hyperbolic-tangent model shows a poorer statistical performance for the combined data. Despite these differences in the model constraints, the inferred transition redshift $z_T$ remains relatively stable among the three models and data combinations. Our results show that the departures from the $Λ$CDM model indicated by DESI analyses are not a generic feature of $f(T)$ gravity, but depend strongly on the specific modified gravity parameterization and on the combination of cosmological observations.
